en.name: Grapeseed oil
en.summary: Grapeseed oil keeps 1 year from purchase in a cool dark cupboard with the cap tight. It is highly polyunsaturated, which is exactly why it is the oil in this cupboard you should buy in small bottles: polyunsaturated fat oxidises fastest.
en.pantry: 1 year from purchase, cool, dark, tightly capped. Rancidity is a reaction between oxygen and the double bonds in unsaturated fat, and grapeseed oil is unusually rich in them — far more so than olive or canola. Light, heat, air and time are the four drivers, which is why the shelf above the hob is the worst place in the kitchen and why a half-empty bottle ages faster than a full one: the headspace is a supply of oxygen that grows with every pour. If the bottle you bought is clear glass, decant it or keep it inside a cupboard rather than out on the counter.
en.fridge: No refrigerated timeline is published for grapeseed oil. Refrigeration does slow oxidation and is a defensible choice for a large bottle you use slowly, particularly through a Taiwanese summer — the oil will cloud and thicken in the cold, which is harmless and clears at room temperature. For a bottle in regular use, buying a smaller one does more for quality than chilling a big one.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for grapeseed oil, and freezing is not worth doing. Oil does not set solid the way water does, so there is no convenience gained, and a bottle moved in and out of a freezer collects condensation — water in an oil bottle is a real problem, because it gives spoilage organisms a foothold in a food that otherwise offers them none.
en.thawing: Let a chilled bottle stand at room temperature until it is clear and pours freely. Do not warm it on the hob or in hot water; heat is one of the things that ages an oil.
spoilage: A sharp, crayon or paint-like smell — rancid oil, and decisive.
A bitter, scratchy finish at the back of the throat.
A sticky, varnish-like film around the neck and cap.
Colour noticeably darker or duller than when the bottle was opened.
tips: Buy small bottles; this is the oil least forgiving of a slow half-bottle.
Never store it above the hob.
Smell it before using it in a dressing, where there is nothing to hide behind.

faq.q: How long does grapeseed oil last?
faq.a: 1 year from purchase in a cool dark cupboard with the cap tight.

faq.q: Why does grapeseed oil go rancid faster than olive oil?
faq.a: It is much more polyunsaturated, and it is the double bonds in unsaturated fat that oxygen attacks. More double bonds means faster rancidity.
No timeline is published for it, but refrigeration slows oxidation and suits a large bottle used slowly. It will cloud in the cold, which is harmless.

zh.name: 葡萄籽油
zh.summary: 葡萄籽油自購買日起，放陰涼避光、瓶蓋鎖緊，可放 1 年。它的多元不飽和脂肪含量很高——而這正是整個油櫃裡最該買小瓶的那一瓶，因為多元不飽和脂肪氧化得最快。
zh.pantry: 自購買日起 1 年，陰涼、避光、鎖緊瓶蓋。油耗是氧氣和不飽和脂肪裡雙鍵的反應，而葡萄籽油的雙鍵特別多——遠多於橄欖油或芥花油。光、熱、空氣和時間是四個推手，所以爐台上方的層架是全廚房最糟的位置；也因此半空的瓶子比滿瓶老得快：那段頂空是每倒一次就變大的氧氣來源。如果你買的是透明玻璃瓶，請分裝或收進櫃子，不要擺在檯面上。
zh.fridge: 葡萄籽油沒有公布的冷藏期限。冷藏確實能拖慢氧化，對一瓶用得慢的大容量是說得過去的選擇，尤其是撐過台灣的夏天——低溫下油會變濁、變稠，那是無害的，回到室溫就清了。但如果是天天在用的那瓶，與其把大瓶冰起來，不如直接買小瓶，對品質的幫助更大。
zh.freezer: 葡萄籽油沒有公布的冷凍期限，冷凍也不值得。油不像水那樣會凍成硬塊，所以使用上沒有任何方便；而一瓶進出冷凍的油只會一直結露——油瓶裡有水是真正的問題，因為它在一個本來什麼都不提供的食物裡，給了腐敗菌立足點。
zh.thawing: 把冰過的瓶子放室溫，等它恢復清澈、倒得順即可。不要拿去爐火上或泡熱水加溫；熱正是讓油老化的原因之一。
spoilage: 聞起來刺鼻、像蠟筆或油漆味——油耗了，而且是決定性的。
入口後喉頭有苦味和刮喉感。
瓶頸和瓶蓋周圍出現黏黏、像亮光漆的膜。
顏色比剛開瓶時明顯變深或變濁。
tips: 買小瓶；這是最禁不起「半瓶慢慢用」的一種油。
絕對不要放在爐台上方。
拿來做沙拉醬前先聞一下，那裡沒有任何味道可以遮掩它。

faq.a: 自購買日起，陰涼避光、瓶蓋鎖緊，1 年。

faq.q: 葡萄籽油為什麼比橄欖油更快油耗？
faq.a: 它的多元不飽和脂肪多得多，而氧氣攻擊的正是不飽和脂肪裡的雙鍵。雙鍵越多，油耗越快。
它沒有公布冷藏期限，但冷藏能拖慢氧化，適合用得慢的大瓶裝。低溫下會變濁，那是無害的。
